status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026 and not yet checked by the translation workers. Vocabulary follows the course: bis, mobil, gadis. Everyday saya and kamu.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Said as It Is Written, Part 1
lessons.description: Every letter is said, and nearly always the same way. Read satu, dua, tiga, and empat aloud, and you have said them right.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Letter C, Part 1
lessons.description: The letter c is always the ch of chair, never a k or an s. Hear it in cinta, cantik, kucing, and kecil.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Ng and Ny, Part 1
lessons.description: Ng is the sound at the end of sing, and ny is the ny of canyon. Either can begin a word. Hear orang, tangan, nyanyi, and nyamuk.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Two Sounds of E, Part 1
lessons.description: The letter e has two sounds: a short murmur in enam and besar, and a clear eh in meja and sore.

lessons.title: Patterns - The Verb Never Says Who, Part 1
lessons.description: An Indonesian verb does not change for who is doing it. Only the word in front says who is going: saya, kamu, dia, kami.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One, Part 1
lessons.description: To make it plain that there is more than one, say the word twice: anak is a child, and anak-anak is children.

lessons.title: Patterns - Done, Doing, and Going To, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb has no tenses. A small word in front of it says when: sudah for done, sedang for right now, and akan for later.

lessons.title: Patterns - Whose It Is, Part 1
lessons.description: The owner comes after the thing owned: my house is house I, rumah saya.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: Put apakah in front of a statement and it becomes a yes-or-no question. Nothing else moves.
words: This is the bus to Jakarta.
Is this the bus to Jakarta?

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: Indonesian has two words for not: tidak for doing and describing, and bukan for things.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come After, Part 1
lessons.description: In English the describing word comes first: a white house. In Indonesian it comes after: rumah putih.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - No Word for Is, Part 1
lessons.description: Indonesian simply leaves out am, is, and are. She is a doctor is she doctor.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb pergi, to go, at work in whole sentences. It is the same pergi every time, whoever is going.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. The answer drops apakah, and a no adds tidak.
words: No, I do not speak English.
Tidak, saya tidak berbicara bahasa Inggris.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: The thing, then itu for the, then what it is like, with no word for is.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways. The verb pergi never changes: the day word says when, and akan marks what is still to come.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
I am going to the market today.
Hari ini saya pergi ke pasar.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
Besok saya akan pergi ke pasar.
